introduction: India has the second-largest road network in the world (after the USA). Road transport is crucial because it provides 'door-to-door' service and acts as a feeder to other modes of transport like railways and airways. In India, roads are classified based on their capacity and the authority responsible for their maintenance.

core_concepts.title: National Highways (NH)
core_concepts.description: These are the primary road networks connecting major cities, capitals, and ports across states. They are constructed and maintained by the Central Government, specifically the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

core_concepts.title: State Highways (SH)
core_concepts.description: These roads connect state capitals with district headquarters and other important cities within a state. They are constructed and maintained by the State Public Works Department (PWD).

core_concepts.title: District and Rural Roads
core_concepts.description: District roads connect district headquarters with other places in the district (maintained by Zila Parishads). Rural roads (the largest category by length) connect villages to towns and are heavily funded by the 'Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana' (PMGSY).

core_concepts.title: Border Roads Organisation (BRO)
core_concepts.description: Established in 1960, the BRO is a highly specialized organization under the Ministry of Defence. It is responsible for constructing and maintaining roads in the difficult, high-altitude terrain of India's northern and northeastern borders.

important_entities.name: NHAI (National Highways Authority of India)
important_entities.significance: NHAI is the nodal agency of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. It is responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of National Highways entrusted to it.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common exam question: Students assume National Highways make up a huge part of India's roads. In reality, National Highways constitute only about '2%' of the total road network length, but they carry a massive '40%' of the total road traffic.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: NH = Central, SH = State, Border = Army
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always link National to NHAI (Central Gov), State to PWD (State Gov), and Border roads directly to the Ministry of Defence (BRO).

exam_strategy_tips: BRO's establishment year (1960) is frequently asked in defense and state-level exams.
If asked which transport mode has the highest share of passenger and freight traffic in India, the answer is 'Roadways' (not Railways).
